finding.title: Replace source-text-grep assertions with real widget tests in t3_readonly_surfaces_gating_test.dart and r3_shell_revocation_exit_test.dart
finding.why: These tests call File(...).readAsStringSync() and assert expect(src, contains('token')) against the raw source text of 5 other-feature screens (app_shell.dart, settings_screen.dart, learning_screen.dart, dashboard_body.dart, text_display_screen.dart). A string search passes whenever the token appears anywhere in the file — in a comment, on an inverted condition, or on unreachable code. Concretely: if a future edit flips the Add Track CTA gate to `!canEditStages`, moves the `if (!isTutoredSession)` guard so UserProfileHeaderCard (the tutor's own sign-out/delete-account surface) renders during a tutored session again (this already shipped once, per the file's own 'BUG 2' comment), or removes the MarkLiveCompletionUseCase call from the live-mark button's onPressed while leaving the string 'MarkLiveCompletionUseCase' in an unrelated comment, every one of these 24 test blocks (23 in t3 across AC1-AC5 plus TUT-04, 1 block/3 assertions in r3's self-labelled 'Structural tests (source-level)' group) keeps passing. Repo-wide grep confirms no other test file references isTutorElevated/isTutoredSession for these screens, so this is the SOLE regression coverage for tutor-mode UI gating outside the tutoring feature. r3's other 3 tests in the same file are genuine provider-level regression tests and are not affected by this finding.
finding.recommendation: Convert each assertion to a widget test that pumps the real screen with canEditStages/isTutoredSession toggled via provider overrides and asserts the CTA/surface is actually present or absent in the render tree — the pattern r3's own first 3 tests and every other l1 test in this batch already use correctly. Delete r3's redundant structural block once covered, or replace it with a widget-level assertion.
acceptance_criteria: Each AC1-AC5 group in t3_readonly_surfaces_gating_test.dart is a testWidgets pumping the real screen and asserting on Finder/rendered output, not File.readAsStringSync() text
A regression test fails if the `if (!isTutoredSession)` guard is removed from UserProfileHeaderCard in settings_screen.dart (BUG 2 class)
A regression test fails if learning_screen.dart's Add Track CTA gate is inverted to `!canEditStages`

finding.title: Remove dead isShabbos/isYomTov/formatHebrewDate from HebrewCalendarUtils (superseded by zmanim_window_service)
finding.rule: Evans lens (ubiquitous language re-derived, not enforced in one place) + dead code

evidence.quote: /// For precise zmanim (sunset/nightfall), use ComplexZmanimCalendar with a GeoLocation.

finding.why: `grep -rn` across all of lib/ finds zero production callers of isShabbos, isYomTov, or formatHebrewDate outside their own definition file — only test/core/utils/hebrew_calendar_utils_test.dart and one story-acceptance test call isShabbos, testing code nothing else ever runs. Meanwhile lib/features/sacred_time/domain/services/zmanim_window_service.dart implements the real, GeoLocation/zmanim-aware Shabbos+Yom-Tov window (candle-lighting offset, tzais, JewishCalendar.isAssurBemelacha) that actually drives the Sacred Time lock feature — and isShabbos's own doc comment admits its 18:00-local-clock-hour heuristic is inferior ("For precise zmanim... use ComplexZmanimCalendar with a GeoLocation"). Because this dead code lives in core/utils/ (importable by any feature — Rule 1 only blocks core→features, not the reverse) and is unit-tested (making it look supported), a future feature needing "is it Shabbos right now" is one natural-language search away from wiring up the crude, timezone-naive version instead of the correct geo-aware one — and if the caller passes a UTC DateTime (the P5-mandated storage format everywhere else in this codebase), isShabbos's `.hour >= 18` check reads UTC hour, not true local hour, silently wrong for any locale far from UTC.
finding.recommendation: Delete isShabbos, isYomTov, and formatHebrewDate (and their test coverage) from HebrewCalendarUtils. If a lightweight non-geo fallback is genuinely wanted somewhere, rename it to make the approximation explicit (e.g. isApproximateShabbosNoGeo) and doc-link to zmanim_window_service.dart as the source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "isShabbos\|isYomTov\|formatHebrewDate" learning_tracker/lib/` shows zero references outside sacred_time/ (or the methods are removed entirely).
hebrew_calendar_utils_test.dart's corresponding groups are removed alongside the source methods.

finding.title: Add regression tests for GoalRepositoryImpl's not-found and delete-sync payload paths
finding.rule: EH-2 (typed exceptions surfaced correctly) / TQ-8 (every reachable error branch needs a red-first test)

evidence.quote:
if (existing == null) {
        throw ArgumentError('Goal not found: $goalId');

finding.why: (a) updateGoal throws ArgumentError when goalId doesn't exist (e.g. the goal was deleted from another device and the sync merge already removed the local row before this device's in-flight edit lands) — no test in this file ever calls updateGoal with a nonexistent id, so nothing pins whether it throws, what it throws, or that a future refactor doesn't silently swallow/change it. (b) The file's own 'sync payload completeness (R4-6)' group exists specifically because create/update once shipped without profile_id/id in the outbox payload — but that hardening was never extended to deleteGoal: _RecordingGoalSyncFacade.deleteGoal is a blind no-op with no payload recorder (unlike goalPayloads for pushGoal), and the sole 'deleteGoal removes the goal' test uses the sync-less `repo` instance, so _syncDeleteGoal's {firestore_id, curriculum_id} payload is completely unverified. A key rename or dropped field in _syncDeleteGoal would ship silently — the exact class of bug R4-6 was written to catch for create/update.
finding.recommendation: Add a test asserting updateGoal(goalId: <nonexistent>) throws ArgumentError; add a deletePayloads recorder to _RecordingGoalSyncFacade and a test asserting deleteGoal() pushes the expected firestore_id/curriculum_id payload, mirroring the existing R4-6 create/update tests.
acceptance_criteria: New red-first test fails against a deliberately-broken updateGoal (e.g. the null check removed) and passes against current code.
New deleteGoal-payload test fails if _syncDeleteGoal's field names are renamed or dropped, mirroring the existing R4-6 create/update tests.

finding.title: Fix the always-passing awk comparison in Makefile check 15/15 (no-cross-feature-deep-imports)

evidence.quote: match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print

finding.why: match($0, ...) scans the whole 'path:lineno:content' grep line and matches the FIRST 'features/xxx/' occurrence, which is always inside the file-path prefix — identical to what match($1, ...) already extracted. a[1] and b[1] are therefore always equal and the filter never prints, regardless of which feature is actually imported. Running the exact command directly against the current tree confirms 0 output even though the 18 cross-feature-import lines cited in the paired finding (and ~26 total repo-wide) exist. Rule 2 has had zero real enforcement, even as a warning, since this check was written.
finding.recommendation: Match the import path portion only (e.g. split on the literal single-quote around the package path before matching, or grep the content field explicitly by re-slicing on the first two colons). Add a fixture case to the audit's own coverage so a future edit to this check can't silently break it again.
acceptance_criteria: Running the check-15/15 grep+awk pipeline against a temporary file containing a known deep cross-feature import produces WARN output instead of silently passing
After the fix, `make audit` output for the current tree lists the auth_validators.dart / onboarding_screen.dart cross-feature imports from finding 3
